prompt: Write a command to get the current SharePoint web and display only its Title and Url properties.
hints: Start with Get-PnPWeb to get the current web object.
Pipe to Select-Object to choose specific properties.
The properties to select are Title and Url.

validation.hintOnFail: Use Get-PnPWeb to retrieve the current web.
Pipe the result using | to another cmdlet.
Use Select-Object to choose which properties to display.

explanation: Get-PnPWeb returns the current web object. Piping to Select-Object Title, Url filters the output to show only those two properties.

prompt: Write the command to create a new team site with the title 'Marketing' and the alias 'Marketing'.

validation.hintOnFail: Specify -Type TeamSite to create a team site.

explanation: New-PnPSite -Type TeamSite creates a team site backed by a Microsoft 365 Group. The -Alias sets the group email prefix and site URL path.

prompt: Write the command to create a new SharePoint list called 'Tasks' using the GenericList template.
hints: The -Title parameter sets the list name.
The -Template parameter specifies the list type.
explanation: New-PnPList creates a new list on the connected SharePoint site. GenericList creates a standard custom list with a Title column.

prompt: Write the command to add a text column called 'Department' (internal name 'Department') to the 'Tasks' list.

validation.hintOnFail: Specify -List "Tasks" to target the Tasks list.
Set -Type to Text for a text column.

explanation: Add-PnPField adds a new column to an existing list. The -InternalName is used in code and CAML queries, while -DisplayName is what users see in the browser.
